title: Scorecard weights
decision: Propensity score = usage growth {w_usage} + new builders {w_newdev} + SA engagement {w_eng} + On-track % {w_burn}, each measured as a percentile against all accounts.
why: Usage growth is the clearest sign a customer is already moving work onto the platform, so it counts most.
possibly: Possibly we can replace hand-set weights with a model trained on which accounts actually grew.

title: 90-day window
decision: Usage growth and SA meetings look back {win_usage} days; new builders look back {win_newdev} days.
why: A quarter smooths out weekly noise but still reflects today. New teams show up fast, so a month catches them early.
possibly: Possibly we can test 30, 60 and 90-day windows and keep the one that best predicts growth.

title: Pool of funds formula
decision: Pool of funds = unused commit + open pipeline. Opportunity value = Propensity score ÷ 100 × Pool of funds.
why: Unused commit protects the renewal and open deals are new revenue; together they are the money our help could unlock. The Propensity score is used as a rough likelihood, not a calibrated probability.
possibly: Possibly we can calibrate the score against past win rates so Opportunity value reads as real expected dollars.

title: Team capacity
decision: The team can actively cover the top {capacity} accounts by Opportunity value.
why: The team is a fixed size, so dedicated help goes where Opportunity value is highest; everyone else gets a scaled type of help.
possibly: Possibly we can set team capacity from real SA/FDE hours per engagement instead of a flat count.

title: Alert thresholds
decision: Commit at Risk: On-track % below {car_pace} after {car_min_elapsed} of the contract. Days to renewal: within {renewal_days} days. Usage Spike: {spike}× normal. New builders: {newdev_min}+ in {win_newdev} days.
why: Each alert is a "why now" signal tied to an action: catch up on commit, prepare the renewal, support a launch, or onboard a new team.
possibly: Possibly we can tune each threshold so it fires only as often as the team can act on it each week.

title: On-track bands
decision: On track at {on_track_good}+; Slightly behind from {on_track_warn} to just under {on_track_good}; Behind below {on_track_warn}.
why: Small gaps tend to close on their own; below {on_track_warn} the customer usually needs help to use the commit, so the Behind band matches the Commit at Risk alert.
possibly: Possibly we can adjust On-track % for seasonal industries like retail (Q4 peaks) using spending curves from similar customers.

title: Type-of-help cut-offs
decision: High Propensity score = {score_high}+; big Pool of funds = {pool_high}+. Together they pick one of four types of help.
why: Splitting likelihood from size stops big-but-unlikely and small-but-likely accounts from getting the same help.
possibly: Possibly we can revisit the cut-offs each quarter as team capacity and the customer base change.

title: Comparison group
decision: {holdout_share} of Commit Burn Sprint accounts are picked at random, measured, but not enrolled.
why: Comparing helped vs. similar unhelped customers shows the program's real impact, not growth that would have happened anyway.
possibly: Possibly we can rotate the comparison group each cycle so no customer goes without help for long.
